local_elby_dashboard · RISE

RISE Learner → Moodle User Provisioning

Turn NESA-approved RISE applicants into real Moodle accounts — keeping the existing sequential {type}{yy}{seq} username and writing the NID into idnumber — then SMS the learner a password-reset link, alert them by SMS when their identity data needs fixing, expose account state and a manual "create account" action in the learners table, and badge RISE learners on their profile page. Course enrolment is deferred.

📦 Plugin: local_elby_dashboard 🧩 Moodle 5.0+ ⚛ Preact + PHP external API 🗓 Plan drafted 2026-07-07

▤Current state (what we build on)

RISE review pipeline

  • rise.php hosts a Preact SPA (amd/src/components/Rise.tsx).
  • NESA reviews live in elby_rise_reviews (unique on campaignid+applicantid), carrying a full JSON snapshot of the applicant plus nesastatus, nesaindexnumber, nidstatus, nidverified, nid, fullname.
  • Approvals flow through external\rise::save_review(); NIDA identity comparison through validate_nid().

Existing account-creation pattern

  • external\signup::register_sdms_user() already creates Moodle users via user_create_user() — reuse its shape (username, firstname/lastname split, auth='manual', confirmed=1, mnethostid).
  • Rwandan name convention helper parse_sdms_names() (first token = lastname) is reusable.
  • Frontend talks to the backend only via ajaxCall(methodname, args) → core/ajax; the API key never reaches the browser.
Key insight: the review row is already the per-applicant system-of-record on the Moodle side. It is the natural place to store the resulting userid, making "does this learner have an account?" a single indexed lookup.
Production reality (confirmed): many learners already have Moodle accounts with idnumber set to their NID but not linked to any RISE review row. So the dominant operation is link an existing user by NID, not create a new one — matching-by-idnumber is the primary path (below), and the backfill task is mostly a linking sweep.

▦Data model changes

One new column links a review to its provisioned Moodle user; plus lightweight action-state tracking.

install.xml + upgrade.php New fields on elby_rise_reviews

State is split into distinct fields (per review) so provisioning state, correction state and notification-dedupe state never overload one column:

FieldTypePurpose
useridint(10), null, FK → user.idProvisioned/linked Moodle user. NULL = no account yet.
provisioningactionchar(32), nullLearner-facing provisioning state: ok, nid_missing, nid_invalid, details_mismatch, duplicate_nid.
correctionstatuschar(20), nullReviewer-facing correction state: none → resubmitted → reviewed.
lastnotifiedhashchar(40), nullSHA-1 of the last notification payload (nesastatus, comment, provisioningaction) — dedupes payloads, but must be combined with an active-token check (a resend is forced when no unexpired, unused correction token exists, even if the hash is unchanged).
lastnotifiedatint(10), default 0When the last SMS/bell notification was sent.
userprovisionedatint(10), default 0Timestamp the account was created/linked.
risesyncstatuschar(20), default 'ok'RISE linkedUserId back-write state: ok, pending, error, conflict — the backfill task retries pending/error.
risesyncerrortext, nullLast RISE PATCH error detail (audit/diagnostics).
risesyncedatint(10), default 0When the linkedUserId back-write last succeeded.
riselinkeduseridchar(32), nullWhat RISE currently reports as linkedUserId (detects conflicts before overwriting).

new table elby_rise_tokens (set-password & correction links)

One table backs both the set-password link and the correction deep link. Only a hash of the token is stored; the raw token travels in the SMS URL and is looked up by hash — so tokens are secure-random, single-use, time-limited and revocable.

FieldTypePurpose
idint, PK—
purposechar(20)setpassword | correction
tokenhashchar(64), uniqueSHA-256 of the secure-random raw token (never the raw value).
campaignid / applicantidcharWho the link is for.
useridint, nullSet for setpassword tokens.
expiresint(10)Hard expiry (e.g. +72h for correction, +24h for set-password).
usedatint(10), default 0Non-zero once consumed — enforces single-use.
timecreatedint(10)Audit.

new table elby_rise_username_seq (portable, collision-free sequence)

Replaces the non-portable CAST(username AS UNSIGNED) / MAX()+1 approach. One row per {type}{yy} prefix; incremented inside a Moodle Lock so concurrent approvals never mint the same username, on any DB engine.

FieldTypePurpose
seqkeychar(8), uniquePrefix, e.g. 126 (learner+2026).
nextvalint(10)Next sequence number to assign.
One-time seed (portable): the upgrade step seeds nextval per prefix without DB-specific casts — fetch candidate usernames with username LIKE '126%' and parse the numeric suffix in PHP to find the max, then nextval = max+1. No CAST(... AS UNSIGNED) in the seed either.

new table elby_rise_corrections (learner re-submissions)

FieldTypePurpose
idint, PK— (also the file itemid for the two uploads)
campaignid / applicantidcharTies the correction to the RISE applicant + its review row.
firstname / lastname / nidcharLearner-corrected values.
notetext, nullLearner's reply to the reviewer.
statuschar(20)pending → reviewed; drives the "resubmitted" pill.
reviewedby / reviewedatint, nullWho cleared the resubmission and when (audit).
timecreated / timemodifiedintUploaded files live in fileareas rise_idcard / rise_nesaresult, itemid = this id.

Why keep state on the review row? Every provisioning trigger (approval or manual) already guarantees a review row exists, and a learner is uniquely one applicant. Co-locating the split state fields with the snapshot/decision avoids a join; tokens, corrections and the username sequence live in their own tables because they are one-to-many or security-sensitive.

⚙Provisioning rules (the decision table)

A single class, classes/rise_user_service.php, owns all identity → account logic so the endpoint, the approval hook and the backfill task share one code path.

Matching & idempotency

  1. Already linked? If review.userid is set and the user exists → no-op, return existing.
  2. Match by NID (primary path in production): look up active users where idnumber = nid AND deleted = 0, then apply the duplicate-NID rules below.
  3. Create (fallback): only when no active user carries that idnumber, create via user_create_user().

Duplicate-NID / conflict rules (explicit)

SituationAction
Exactly one active user has the NID, not yet linkedLink (store userid). If their name disagrees with the server-fetched RISE applicant (get_applicant(), not the browser snapshot) → still link, flag details_mismatch.
Multiple active users share the NIDBlock, set duplicate_nid, surface to the reviewer to resolve — never guess.
Matching user is already linked to a different review/applicantBlock, set duplicate_nid; a real person maps to one applicant — flag for manual resolution.
Only match is deleted/suspendedDeleted → ignore (treat as no match, create). Suspended → link but flag for reviewer (do not silently re-activate).
Because user.idnumber = nid is the join key on both sides, the table's account-status lookup (status_for()) resolves existing accounts by idnumber IN (nids) even for learners never yet reviewed — surfacing "already has an account" without any prior link.
Identity source is RISE, not the review snapshot (mandatory). The current review snapshot is browser-supplied — save_review() stores fullname/nid/phone/applicantdata straight from the frontend PARAM_RAW payload (Rise.tsx → JSON.stringify(applicant)). Therefore provisioning identity must come from rise_client::get_applicant($applicantid) (server-side, X-API-KEY — verified working). The snapshot is a display/cache fallback only and must not feed user.idnumber, Moodle names, phone/SMS, or the RISE linkedUserId update unless it was refreshed from RISE in the same request/job. create_user/provision fail closed if the fetch fails or returns an applicant whose campaign/status doesn't match the request — never fall back to browser JSON.
Server-authoritative verification. validate_nid() and save_review(nidverified) currently trust frontend-supplied values. Since provisioningaction='ok' depends on NIDA verification, the plan must make verification server-authoritative — re-derive NID/name/DOB from get_applicant() and (re)run the TMIS/NIDA check server-side rather than trusting nidverified from the browser.
Native bi-directional link + back-write semantics. RISE applicants carry linkedUserId; on successful provisioning, write the Moodle userid back via rise_client::patch_applicant($id, ['linkedUserId'=>$userid]) and optionally read it as a secondary match signal. Consistency rules: Moodle is source of truth — if user creation succeeds but the RISE PATCH fails, do not roll back; record a pending-sync/error state on the review row and retry via the backfill task. Make the PATCH idempotent, and if RISE already holds a different non-empty linkedUserId, treat it as a conflict (flag for the reviewer) rather than overwriting.

Action-code evaluation (drives notifications & the profile badge)

ConditionAction codeCreate account?Learner sees

NID empty on the snapshotnid_missingYes (idnumber blank)"Add your National ID"
NID present but not a 16-digit numbernid_invalidYes"Fix your National ID number"

Note: creating the account is deliberately never blocked by a bad NID (except a true duplicate/conflict). We provision, set idnumber best-effort, and raise a provisioningaction the learner resolves — this satisfies "must have an account" while still surfacing the fix.
NID validation scope: the plan validates 16-digit numeric format only. A Rwanda NID checksum is not assumed — if a confirmed checksum algorithm is available it can tighten nid_invalid later; identity correctness is otherwise established by the existing NIDA (validate_nid()) comparison, not a local checksum.

Username generation (confirmed from production)

Existing prod RISE accounts use a manually generated 8-digit sequential username (verified rows: 12609278, 12600693, with the 16-digit NID in idnumber, auth=manual). We keep generating the same shape:

SegmentMeaningExample (12609278)
{type}1 digit — 1 = learner, 2 = facilitator1 (learner)
{yy}2-digit intake year26 (2026)
{seq}zero-padded incrementing sequence within that type+year09278
 
// rise_user_service::next_username($type='learner') — portable + concurrency-safe
$prefix = ($type === 'facilitator' ? '2' : '1') . substr(date('Y'), 2, 2);   // '126'
$lockfactory = \core\lock\lock_config::get_lock_factory('local_elby_dashboard_username');
$lock = $lockfactory->get_lock($prefix, 10);                                   // blocks concurrent minting
try {
    $seq = $DB->get_field('elby_rise_username_seq', 'nextval', ['seqkey' => $prefix]);
    if ($seq === false) { $seq = 1; $DB->insert_record('elby_rise_username_seq',
                              (object)['seqkey' => $prefix, 'nextval' => $seq]); }
    // Skip any number already taken (e.g. manually created before this feature).
    do { $username = $prefix . str_pad((string)$seq++, 5, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT); }
    while ($DB->record_exists('user', ['username' => $username]));
    $DB->set_field('elby_rise_username_seq', 'nextval', $seq, ['seqkey' => $prefix]);
} finally { $lock->release(); }
Portable & collision-free: no CAST(username AS UNSIGNED) (which is MySQL-specific). A per-prefix row in elby_rise_username_seq is advanced inside a Moodle Lock, so simultaneous approvals serialise; the inner existence check skips numbers taken by the legacy manual scheme.
Scope for now is learners ({type}=1). Facilitator provisioning ({type}=2) reuses the same generator with a different type argument when needed.
// classes/rise_user_service.php — shape
class rise_user_service {
    public static function split_name(string $fullname): array;        // shared (was signup's private)
    public function find_user(string $nid): array;                     // active users by idnumber=nid
    public function evaluate_action(array $applicant, ?object $rev): string; // 'nid_invalid' | ...
    public function provision(string $campaignid, string $applicantid): array;
        // identity = rise_client::get_applicant($applicantid) server-side; fail-closed
        // on fetch error or campaign/status mismatch. Snapshot is never trusted.
        // -> ['userid'=>.., 'created'=>bool, 'action'=>'ok', 'username'=>.., 'risesync'=>'ok'|'pending']
    public function notify_learner(object $review, string $comment=''): void; // SMS + bell, deduped
    public function send_sms(string $phone, string $message): bool;    // wraps sms_client
    public function status_for(array $pairs, string $campaignid): array; // [{applicantid,nid}] -> status
}

↔Backend: web-service endpoints

Two AJAX external methods added to classes/external/rise.php (registered in db/services.php), plus a normal form-POST page for the correction upload (external AJAX methods are a poor fit for no-login multipart uploads — see the Correction form section).

Web-service functionParamsReturnsCapability
..._rise_get_user_status new campaignid, pairs[] of {applicantid, nid} JSON keyed by applicantid → {hasaccount, userid, username, provisioningaction, correctionstatus, profileurl} viewreports
..._rise_create_user new campaignid, applicantid (only) JSON {success, userid, username, action, message} viewreports + new manageriseusers
Never trust browser identity data. create_user takes only applicantid and provisions from a server-side rise_client::get_applicant($applicantid) fetch. It fails closed if the fetch errors or the returned applicant's campaign/status doesn't match the request — it never falls back to the (browser-supplied) review snapshot. A privileged frontend must not be able to submit altered names/NIDs/phones.
Moodle external param shape for pairs[]. Existing RISE methods use flat external_values. get_user_status needs a structured param: an external_multiple_structure(new external_single_structure(['applicantid'=>…,'nid'=>…])) — or accept a single PARAM_RAW JSON string and decode server-side. The plan uses the structured form.
Why {applicantid, nid} pairs for status? Unreviewed learners have no elby_rise_reviews row, so the backend has no NID to match on from an applicant id alone. The NID travels with each pair (already visible to the reviewer in the applicant list) so status_for() can resolve existing accounts via idnumber IN (nids). (Alternatively the backend re-fetches applicant NIDs from RISE server-side.)
New capability local/elby_dashboard:manageriseusers — full source plumbing. Today db/access.php only defines view/viewreports/manage, and rise.php passes only isAdmin. Add every touchpoint: (1) the capability in db/access.php (write, CONTEXT_SYSTEM, RISK_PERSONAL, manager archetype); (2) its lang string elby_dashboard:manageriseusers; (3) the new functions in both $functions and the local_elby_dashboard_service list in db/services.php; (4) require_capability() inside the PHP endpoint methods (not only the services metadata); (5) a canManageRiseUsers flag in the data rise.php passes to the SPA (alongside isAdmin); (6) frontend hide/disable of the create buttons when false.

✓Auto-provision on NESA approval

The one behavioural change to the existing review flow.

In external\rise::save_review(), after the review row is inserted/updated, when nesastatus === 'approved' call the provisioning service. Failures must not roll back the saved decision — provisioning is logged and retriable (the backfill task and the manual button both recover it).

Capability tightening (required). save_review() currently only requires local/elby_dashboard:viewreports. Since approval now creates Moodle accounts, guard the provisioning step with has_capability('local/elby_dashboard:manageriseusers', $context): reviewers with the manage capability provision immediately; a reviewer without it can still record the decision, but provisioning is deferred to the backfill task rather than performed under read-only rights. Account creation is never reachable with report-only access.
// external/rise.php :: save_review(), after $DB->update_record/insert_record
if ($data->nesastatus === 'approved'
        && has_capability('local/elby_dashboard:manageriseusers', $context)) {
    try {
        $svc = new \local_elby_dashboard\rise_user_service();
        $svc->provision($data->campaignid, $data->applicantid);   // re-fetches identity via get_applicant()
    } catch (\Throwable $e) {
        debugging('RISE provisioning failed: ' . $e->getMessage(), DEBUG_DEVELOPER);
    }
}
// else: decision saved; backfill task provisions it later.
Idempotent: re-approving or editing an approved review re-runs provision(), which no-ops if already linked and only refreshes the action code / notification.

📱Learner notifications — SMS + password reset

SMS is the primary channel (we have the phone from the RISE record; most learners never open Moodle); the in-Moodle bell is kept as a second channel for logged-in learners. Triggers: a welcome SMS with a set-password link on account creation, and an action-needed SMS+bell (carrying the reviewer comment + form link) when identity data must be fixed.

1. Account-created SMS (custom set-password link)

Core forgot_password.php is email-oriented and won't help learners whose only email is the synthetic @learner.rise.reb.rw address. So define a dedicated set-password flow backed by elby_rise_tokens:

  • On create: generate a random password + set auth_forcepasswordchange; mint a secure-random token (e.g. 32 bytes, random_string/CSPRNG), store only its SHA-256 hash with purpose='setpassword', userid, and expires = now + 24h.
  • SMS the username + a short URL rise_setpassword.php?t={rawtoken}.
  • The page looks the token up by hash, checks not expired and not used (usedat=0), lets the learner set a password (subject to check_password_policy), then marks usedat=time() (single-use).
  • Controls: rate-limit the page (shared helper — below), audit each mint/consume, and show clear invalid / expired / already-used messaging with a "request a new link" path.

2. Review-saved SMS (reviewer comment + form link)

  • Trigger: whenever a review is saved with a decision that needs the learner to act — action_requested, rejected, or an approved-with-issues action code. Fired from save_review().
  • Body: the reviewer's comment (the comment field the NESA reviewer typed) + a deep link to the learner correction form (below). E.g. "NESA review: <comment>. Update your details here: <link>".
  • De-dupe via stored state: compute hash = sha1(nesastatus.comment.provisioningaction); send only if it differs from lastnotifiedhash, then update lastnotifiedhash/lastnotifiedat.
  • Token-aware resend (important): correction links expire and are single-use, so hash-only dedupe can strand a learner with a dead link when the reviewer re-saves the same comment/action. Always send (minting a fresh token) when there is no active, unexpired, unused correction token — fold token validity into the dedupe decision, not just the payload hash. Full send history lives in elby_rise_sms_log.

3. In-Moodle bell notification (kept)

  • Create db/messages.php (new file — the plugin has none today) declaring a riseaction message provider, add the messageprovider:riseaction lang string, and send a matching \core\message\message to the learner's account when one exists. Decide default popup/email behaviour deliberately — accounts have a synthetic @learner.rise.reb.rw email, so email delivery is effectively a no-op; popup (bell) is the meaningful channel. Its contexturl points at the correction form.

Delivery mechanism — InTouch SMS gateway

REB's gateway is InTouch SMS (intouchsms.co.rw), a simple HTTP API with Basic auth. We add a server-side client mirroring the existing rise_client / tmis_client (Moodle \curl, config-driven credentials, retries) — no credentials ever reach the browser.

AspectValue (from the test call)
EndpointGET https://www.intouchsms.co.rw/api/sendsms/.json
AuthAuthorization: Basic <base64(sms_username:sms_password)> — credentials from plugin config only
Query paramssender (e.g. REB), message (URL-encoded), recipients (comma-separated)
Recipient formatLocal 07XXXXXXXX — not E.164
 
// classes/sms_client.php  — pattern-matches rise_client/tmis_client
class sms_client {
    public function __construct() {
        $this->baseurl  = get_config('local_elby_dashboard','sms_api_url')
                          ?: 'https://www.intouchsms.co.rw/api/sendsms/.json';
        $this->sender   = get_config('local_elby_dashboard','sms_sender') ?: 'REB';
        $this->user     = get_config('local_elby_dashboard','sms_username');  // server-side only
        $this->password = get_config('local_elby_dashboard','sms_password');
    }
    public function send(string $phone, string $message): bool {
        $to = self::normalise_rw($phone);            // -> 07XXXXXXXX, else null => skip+flag
        if (!$to) { return false; }
        $curl = new \curl();
        $curl->setHeader(['Authorization: Basic ' . base64_encode($this->user.':'.$this->password)]);
        $url = $this->baseurl . '?' . http_build_query(
                 ['sender'=>$this->sender,'message'=>$message,'recipients'=>$to],
                 '', '&', PHP_QUERY_RFC3986);
        $curl->get($url);
        return ((int)($curl->get_info()['http_code'] ?? 0)) === 200;
    }
}
  • Phone normalisation normalise_rw(): strip spaces/+; map 2507XXXXXXXX / +2507… → 07XXXXXXXX; validate it's a 10-digit 07 number, else skip and flag nid/phone action so it isn't silently dropped.
  • A thin rise_user_service::send_sms($phone,$message) wraps the client so the approval hook, manual button, review-save trigger and backfill all share one path (and one place to add logging/retry).
Two channels, one payload: SMS (InTouch) is the primary/required channel; the in-Moodle bell is the second channel for logged-in learners. Both carry the reviewer comment and the same correction-form link.
Credentials: store the InTouch sms_username/sms_password, sms_sender and endpoint in plugin settings (see below); never hard-code or document real/test credentials. Add an sms_enabled toggle so SMS can be turned off in dev/staging.

📝Learner self-service correction form

When action is needed, the learner must be able to correct their details and re-submit evidence themselves. This closes the loop: reviewer requests a fix → SMS/bell with the comment + link → learner fixes → reviewer re-reviews.

The form

New learner-facing page rise_action.php (styled like the existing public signup.php). Fields, pre-filled from the applicant snapshot:

FieldTypeNotes
First name / Last nametextPrefilled; learner corrects the spelling/splitting.
National ID (NID)text (16 digits)Client + server format validation; this is what must match NIDA.
National ID documentfile uploadImage/PDF of the ID card.
NESA confirmation of resultsfile uploadNESA Senior-3 result confirmation document.
(optional) notetextareaLearner reply to the reviewer.

Access — two entry points, one secure token

  • SMS / bell deep link (no login required): rise_action.php?t={rawtoken}. The token is a secure-random value stored (hashed) in elby_rise_tokens with purpose='correction', applicantid/campaignid, and expires (e.g. +72h). The page resolves it by hash and checks not expired and not used — so it is genuinely time-limited, single-use and revocable (delete the row). This works before the learner has an account (action_requested/rejected happen pre-approval), mirroring the public, rate-limited signup.php.
  • From the user profile (logged-in): once an account exists, the profile badge links to the same page, authenticated by session (no token needed).
Not a bare HMAC. A static sha256(applicantid.campaignid.secret) never expires and can't be revoked. Use the stored-token table (above) — or, if stateless is preferred, a signed payload carrying applicantid, campaignid, exp and a nonce. The plan uses the stored-token approach for revocability + single-use.

Submission & re-review loop (form POST, not AJAX)

  • rise_action.php handles the submission as a normal server-side form POST (a moodleform with sesskey when logged-in; token-validated when public) — not an external AJAX method, which is a poor fit for no-login multipart uploads.
  • Validate token first, then accept files. Store the two uploads via the File API (component local_elby_dashboard, fileareas rise_idcard / rise_nesaresult, itemid = correction id) after strict checks.
  • Persist to elby_rise_corrections, set the review's correctionstatus = 'resubmitted' (separate from provisioningaction), consume the token (usedat), and optionally re-run validate_nid() with the corrected NID.
  • The reviewer sees the resubmission (pill + uploaded docs in the drawer) and re-reviews; on approval, provisioning updates the linked user's firstname/lastname/idnumber if they changed.
Upload controls (all required): per-file size limit (e.g. ≤ 8 MB); server-side MIME/type validation with an image/PDF allowlist (not just extension); token validated before any file is accepted; rate-limited via a shared helper (below); virus scan via Moodle's antivirus hook if configured.
pluginfile access control (required work item). local_elby_dashboard_pluginfile() today only serves the logo filearea (lib.php:141). Extend it to serve rise_idcard / rise_nesaresult with strict rules: map itemid to a real elby_rise_corrections row; allow a reviewer with local/elby_dashboard:viewreports, or the linked learner themselves, or a request carrying a valid unexpired correction token — never broad/public access to ID documents and results.
Shared rate-limit helper. signup::rate_limit_check() is private (classes/external/signup.php) and can't be called. Extract a shared guard (its cache definition in db/caches.php is reusable) or add distinct cache keys rise_action / rise_setpassword. Do not plan to call the private method.
RISE field write-back — verified on prod. PATCH /api/applicants/{id} (X-API-KEY) is confirmed working: {"fullName":"…"} returns {success:true, applicantUpdated:true, learnerUpdated:true} and RISE auto-propagates to its linked learner record. So when a learner corrects fullName/nid, the handler can push those fields straight back to RISE via a new rise_client::patch_applicant($id, $fields). Note a field whitelist: phone was rejected (applicantUpdated:false) — confirm the exact updatable set before relying on any field beyond fullName/nid.
Deferred: forwarding the uploaded documents back to RISE (the attachmentsPushed path) is a later item. For now, store uploads in Moodle file storage only; the reviewer views them in the applicant drawer. Field (name/NID) write-back above is in scope.

🏷Profile-page badge

Show a "RISE Learner" badge (with verification state) on every user's profile.

Extend the existing local_elby_dashboard_myprofile_navigation() callback in lib.php (it already renders SDMS profile nodes — do not replace it; preserve those nodes and use non-conflicting category/node IDs). Detect a RISE learner by an elby_rise_reviews row where userid = $user->id. Add a node rendering a coloured badge — and, when there is an outstanding action, a "Fix your RISE details" link to the correction form (rise_action.php) beside it:

Review stateBadge
provisioningaction = 'ok', NIDA verified✓ RISE Learner — Verified
provisioningaction is a fixable code (or correctionstatus='resubmitted')⚠ RISE Learner — Action needed
Linked but NID unverifiedRISE Learner
 
// lib.php — ADD to the existing function (keep the SDMS nodes it already builds)
function local_elby_dashboard_myprofile_navigation(
        core_user\output\myprofile\tree $tree, $user, $iscurrentuser, $course) {
    global $DB;
    $rev = $DB->get_record('elby_rise_reviews', ['userid' => $user->id], '*', IGNORE_MULTIPLE);
    if (!$rev) { return; }
    $badge = /* build coloured <span> from $rev->provisioningaction / correctionstatus / nidstatus */;
    $node  = new core_user\output\myprofile\node('contact', 'riselearner',
              get_string('rise_badge_label','local_elby_dashboard'), null, null, $badge);
    $tree->add_node($node);
}

⚛Frontend (Rise.tsx)

Add account visibility + a manual create action to the applicants table and drawer. Built with Vite/pnpm and committed as the rebuilt AMD bundle (matching how dashboard.js ships today).

Applicants table — new ACCOUNT column

  • On load, after fetching applicants, batch-call local_elby_dashboard_rise_get_user_status with the visible {applicantid, nid} pairs; store in a Record<applicantid, UserStatus> state (mirrors the existing reviews map).
  • Render a pill: Account (links to /user/profile.php?id=), Action needed, or a Create account button — the button is shown only when canManageRiseUsers is true (hidden/disabled otherwise).
  • The button's onClick must call event.stopPropagation() (rows open the drawer via their own onClick), then call local_elby_dashboard_rise_create_user and optimistically update the row; disabled + spinner while in flight.
  • Excel export: the export builds its own full, filtered row set via fetchAllFilteredApplicants() — not the visible page — so it needs a second rise_get_user_status batch call over the entire export set to populate the "Account" / "Account action" columns.

Applicant drawer

  • Add an "Account" info block near the NIDA section: shows username + profile link when provisioned, or a primary "Create Moodle account" button (brand #005198, gated on canManageRiseUsers) when not — reusing the confirm-modal style already in NesaReviewSection.
  • Surface the action code inline (e.g. an amber note "National ID needs fixing before this learner can be verified").

Types

// amd/src/types.ts
export interface RiseUserStatus {
    hasaccount: boolean;
    userid: number;
    username: string;
    provisioningaction: 'ok'|'nid_missing'|'nid_invalid'|'details_mismatch'|'duplicate_nid'|'none';
    correctionstatus: 'none'|'resubmitted'|'reviewed';
    profileurl?: string;
}
Frontend mirrors the split backend state: provisioningaction (identity/account fixes) and correctionstatus (learner resubmission) are separate, so a "resubmitted" pill and an "action needed" pill never fight over one field.
Build step: run the plugin's pnpm/Vite build (see package.json / vite.config.ts) and commit the regenerated bundle — recent commits show dashboard.js is rebuilt and versioned alongside source.

🌐Language strings & config

New strings lang/en/local_elby_dashboard.php

  • rise_badge_label, rise_badge_verified, rise_badge_action
  • rise_create_account, rise_account_exists, rise_account_created
  • rise_action_nid_missing, rise_action_nid_invalid, rise_action_details_mismatch, rise_action_duplicate_nid
  • rise_action_prompt, messageprovider:riseaction
  • set-password page: rise_setpassword_title, rise_token_invalid, rise_token_expired, rise_token_used
  • capability strings: elby_dashboard:manageriseusers

New setting settings.php

  • rise_signup_email_domain — default learner.rise.reb.rw, used to synthesise learner emails when the applicant record has none.
  • Optional rise_autoprovision toggle (default on) to disable auto-creation on approval without touching code.
  • SMS (InTouch): sms_enabled, sms_api_url (default https://www.intouchsms.co.rw/api/sendsms/.json), sms_sender (default REB), sms_username, sms_password (password field), sms_timeout.
  • Token/link config: rise_action_link_base (public base URL for SMS links); token lifetimes are constants in code (correction 72h, set-password 24h). No shared HMAC secret needed — tokens are stored, not signed.
Privacy provider + retention (required, currently missing). The plugin has no classes/privacy/provider.php, but this feature adds sensitive personal data: NIDs, phone numbers, review snapshots, tokens, SMS state/logs, and uploaded ID-card / NESA-result documents. Add a privacy provider declaring the new tables (elby_rise_reviews additions, elby_rise_tokens, elby_rise_corrections, elby_rise_sms_log) and fileareas (rise_idcard, rise_nesaresult), plus export/delete support and a retention policy for tokens and uploaded evidence.

▶Delivery plan

1

Schema + split state

New/renamed fields (provisioningaction, correctionstatus, lastnotifiedhash/at, userid, risesyncstatus/error/at, riselinkeduserid), tables (elby_rise_tokens, elby_rise_username_seq, elby_rise_corrections), upgrade.php + seed, version bump.

2

Service (link-first) + tests

rise_user_service: shared split_name(), NID matching with explicit duplicate/conflict rules, server-authoritative get_applicant()-based provision(). Unit-tested.

3

Portable username sequencing

elby_rise_username_seq + Moodle Lock API generator (no CAST), with existence-skip for legacy numbers.

4

Endpoints + hardened capability + hook

Two AJAX methods (get_user_status by {applicantid,nid}, create_user by id only), manageriseusers capability, save_review() hook gated by capability; manual create + backfill share the service.

5

SMS client + notification dedupe

sms_client (InTouch), send_sms() wrapper, db/messages.php bell provider, dedupe via lastnotifiedhash (optional SMS log table).

6

Set-password token flow

elby_rise_tokens mint/consume, rise_setpassword.php (expiry, single-use, hashed storage, rate-limit, clear UX).

7

Correction form + uploads + pluginfile

rise_action.php form-POST handler, token-gated, shared rate-limit helper, File API storage with strict type/size validation, and pluginfile() access rules for rise_idcard/rise_nesaresult; correctionstatus='resubmitted' surfaced to the reviewer.

8

Frontend + profile badge

Account column/drawer, create button, resubmission pill, split-state types; myprofile_navigation() badge + "Fix your details" link; rebuild + commit the bundle.

9

Backfill / link sweep + RISE sync retry

Scheduled/adhoc ensure_rise_users task (classes/task/ + db/tasks.php): for in-scope learners with userid unset, link by idnumber = nid, create only when none matches. Also provisions decisions saved by reviewers lacking the manage capability, and retries pending RISE linkedUserId back-writes.

10

Privacy provider + retention

classes/privacy/provider.php for the new tables + fileareas (export/delete), retention policy for tokens and uploaded evidence. Ship before go-live.

✔Testing checklist

  • Approving a review with a valid 16-digit NID creates a user with idnumber = nid, provisioningaction = ok, and no action-needed notification (a welcome SMS is still sent).
  • Approving with a missing/invalid NID still creates the account and raises nid_missing/nid_invalid + notification.
  • Approving when nidstatus = 'mismatch' raises details_mismatch + notification.
  • Exactly one existing active user with the NID → linked (no new account). Multiple active users with the NID, or a match already linked to another applicant → blocked with duplicate_nid, escalated to the reviewer. Deleted match → creates; suspended match → links + flags.
  • Synthetic email is unique; an applicant-supplied email that collides with an existing user does not break creation or hijack that user.
  • get_user_status resolves an unreviewed learner's existing account from its {applicantid, nid} pair (no review row required).
  • create_user provisions from a server-side get_applicant() fetch and fails closed (no account) if the fetch errors or the applicant's campaign/status doesn't match — never using browser-supplied identity data.
  • On provisioning, the Moodle userid is PATCHed back to RISE linkedUserId; if that PATCH fails the Moodle user is still created and a pending-sync state is retried by the task; an existing different linkedUserId is flagged as a conflict, not overwritten.
  • pluginfile: a reviewer (viewreports), the linked learner, or a valid correction token can view rise_idcard/rise_nesaresult; an anonymous/unauthorised request cannot.
  • Token-aware resend: an expired correction token with an unchanged comment/action still triggers a fresh SMS with a new working link.
  • Excel export populates account columns for every exported row (full-set status fetch), not just the visible page.
  • Create buttons are hidden/disabled without manageriseusers; clicking the row button opens no drawer (stopPropagation).
  • Re-approving / editing an approved review does not create a second account and does not re-notify unless the action changed.
  • New account gets the next sequential {type}{yy}{seq} username from elby_rise_username_seq; two concurrent creates (Lock API) never collide; a number already taken by the legacy manual scheme is skipped.
  • Manual "Create account" button provisions and the table pill flips to Account without reload.
  • Table correctly shows existing-account state for a learner whose NID already matches a Moodle user (link, no button).
  • Profile badge renders the right colour/state for verified / action-needed / linked learners; absent for non-RISE users. When action is pending, the "Fix your details" link opens the correction form.
  • Review saved with action_requested/rejected + a comment sends SMS (and bell, if account exists) containing the reviewer's comment and a working form link.
  • Correction form: valid token opens without login; expired, already-used, or unknown token is rejected with clear UX; NID format validated; uploads pass type/size allowlist and store via File API; submit sets correctionstatus='resubmitted' and consumes the token (second use rejected).
  • Set-password link: valid token lets the learner set a policy-compliant password once; the same token cannot be reused; expired token is rejected; the raw token is never stored (only its hash).
  • After a resubmission, re-approval updates the linked user's firstname/lastname/idnumber if they changed.
  • Account creation sends a welcome SMS with a working password-reset link; learner can set a password and log in.
  • An action-needed change sends an SMS to the learner's phone; no SMS is re-sent when the action code is unchanged; missing/invalid phones are skipped and flagged.
  • Backfill task links/provisions in-scope learners (per the defined criteria), including decisions saved by reviewers without the manage capability, and is safely re-runnable.
  • Capability check: a viewreports-only user can see status and record a decision, but cannot create accounts (provisioning deferred); create_user and provisioning require manageriseusers.
  • upgrade.php applies cleanly from the current version; fields/keys/indexes created.

?Open questions / decisions to confirm

Notification target — resolved. Notifications go to the learner (to fix their own NID / mismatched details). userto = $newuser, userfrom = core_user::get_noreply_user().
Login & username — resolved. Keep the existing sequential {type}{yy}{seq} username scheme; NID stays in idnumber. Learners get a random password + SMS password-reset link to set their own on first login.
SMS gateway — resolved. InTouch SMS (intouchsms.co.rw), Basic auth, local 07… recipients. Only the production sms_username/sms_password need supplying via settings.
Backfill criteria. Confirm which learners the sweep provisions: nesastatus = approved only, remote applicant status = ENROLLED only, or either/both. Plan assumes approved (aligned with "created on approval"); enrolment status is deferred with enrolment.
Facilitators. This plan provisions learners ({type}=1) first. Confirm whether facilitator accounts ({type}=2) are in scope now or later.
RISE PATCH whitelist — blocking pre-implementation check. Confirm the full set of applicant fields PATCH /api/applicants/{id} accepts before relying on correction write-back for NID. Verified on prod: fullName updates (and propagates to the learner); phone is rejected. The write-back assumes fullName + nid — validate nid is writable (and whether NIDA/NESA verification fields are). If nid can't be patched, implement a graceful fallback: store the corrected NID locally, flag it for the reviewer, and do not silently drop it.
Enrolment — deferred. Course/cohort enrolment is explicitly out of scope for now (account creation first); revisit as a follow-up.
